name: Data assistant quality review from real traffic
description: An assistant answering questions against data gets better by impression or not at all. Individual bad answers get noticed and forgotten, so the same failure keeps happening and nobody can say whether last month's fix worked. Group failures by cause rather than reporting single cases, separate a prompt problem from a data problem from a code problem because the fix differs, and come back to measure what actually shipped.

name: Contract review publication and risk alert
description: A completed contract review that only exists inside the reviewer helps nobody. The submitter chases for a verdict, and legal either hears about every routine contract or about none of the risky ones. Decide who this finding is for: publish it where contract records already live, give the submitter a verdict they can act on, and pull legal in only when severity or flag count crosses the line the team drew.

name: Revenue movement report and prediction calibration
description: A revenue report that never checks its own predictions repeats the same mistakes every period, and a report nobody can reconcile against the payment provider is not evidence of anything. State what moved and which products or accounts are behind it, then measure last period's predictions against reality and move the scoring weights from that precision and recall rather than from opinion.

name: Governance drift audit of declarations against code
description: Every declaration in a governed system is a claim about the code. A decision record claims a control exists, a charter claims an agent may reach exactly these tools and no others, a manifest claims a set of checks runs, a baseline claims a number that has been held. Each was true the day it was written and nothing rereads it, so the governance surface slowly becomes an accurate description of a codebase that no longer exists. The worst case is not a claim that fails loudly. It is a check that quietly stopped running while every report continued to say success, which is a failure that looks exactly like health. Read every declaration against the code that would prove it, and keep three verdicts apart: a claim the code confirms, a claim the code refutes, and a claim nothing could have tested either way. Include the checks themselves in the audit rather than trusting their verdicts, because a verifier that can be switched off by the thing it verifies is not one. Then propose every correction and make none of them.

name: Access grant audit and compliance reporting
description: When somebody asks why an access grant was approved, the answer is usually reconstructed by hand from logs, months late, by whoever still remembers. Approval bottlenecks stay invisible in the same way, buried inside an average. Turn one ledger into both the periodic account and any point in time compliance answer, so the two can never disagree, and name the approvers who are slowing the chain instead of letting an average hide them.

name: Contract first API stewardship across three version axes
description: A service has three versions and most teams keep one. The contract it publishes, the routes it actually serves and the artefact it releases each move for their own reason, and collapsing them into a single number makes every one of them wrong: a breaking change ships under a patch bump because the release axis never noticed, a route is served that no consumer could have planned for because it was never published, and a published route answers 404 because it was removed and the document was not. In an organisation where several agents change the same portfolio in the same hour, a single shared version file makes it worse still, because it is a merge conflict by construction and every worker meets it. Keep the published contract, the served routes and the released artefact on three separate axes and in agreement: publish before you serve, move the contract's major only when the contract breaks and carry that break into the route prefix, and move the release on its own trigger. Reconcile in both directions, because a route served but unpublished and a route published but unserved are different defects and only one of them looks like a missing feature.

name: Support issue disposition account
description: Whoever is accountable for a support queue cannot tell from the tracker whether it was handled or merely touched. Without a short account they either open the tracker themselves or stop asking. Say what happened to the issues that were touched, reconciled against the source rather than against local state, and pick the few worth naming instead of counting everything.

name: Issue source coverage and triage
description: A reported issue that nobody looked at again is indistinguishable from one that was handled. Over time the tracker fills with things that are old rather than things that are open, and nobody trusts it enough to read it. Judge whether each issue holds real work, attach a solution already known to work rather than restating the problem, and decide which issues need a person, reading tone and priority together rather than priority alone.

name: Open incident vigilance and escalation
description: Incidents are rarely abandoned deliberately; they go quiet, and without something watching the quiet a serious one sits untouched while a trivial one stays open forever. Decide from the state of the board itself which incidents have been silent longer than their severity allows, and escalate with growing force rather than repeating the same nudge.

name: High intent lead alerting
description: A lead worth a person's time is only worth it while it is still fresh, and an alert that arrives without context makes the person go and reconstruct it themselves. Get the lead in front of whoever should act with enough context to act well, and reserve the more intrusive route for the cases that genuinely earn it.

name: Goal accountability and idea triage review
description: Goals die quietly rather than being abandoned on purpose, captured ideas pile up unreviewed, and decisions that were supposed to be revisited never are. Give an honest trend read on each goal from observed activity rather than from what was said last time, distinguish a goal that is behind from one that has been abandoned, and clear the idea queue instead of letting it grow.

name: Approved maintenance issue filing
description: A maintenance proposal that a person approves and that then goes nowhere is worse than never proposing it, because the approval felt like the work getting done. Turn the approval into a real, findable issue carrying what a maintainer needs to act, and never lose the decision to an API failure.

name: Correspondence drafting and reply review
description: Replies written on someone's behalf either sound generic enough to be noticed or need so much editing that they save nothing, and there is no safe path from assisted to unattended. Compose the reply in that specific recipient's voice, then route it through human review until that contact has earned enough consecutive unedited approvals to graduate, with some categories never graduating regardless of record.

name: Lead welcome email drafting
description: One template sent to everyone reads as a template to everyone, and the person who wrote three sentences about their problem learns immediately that nobody read them. Match the reply to how ready this person actually is, drawing on what they wrote rather than substituting a name into a template.

name: Product idea harvesting from codebase and web
description: Idea harvesting that is not grounded in the product produces plausible-sounding candidates that do not fit what the product is, and triaging them costs more than they are worth. Read what the product actually is before searching, so candidates are plausible for this product rather than generic, and skip vague or meta content instead of passing volume through to triage.

name: Stack-grounded implementation opportunity research
description: Nobody reads release feeds for the dependencies they actually run, so upstream changes that would matter arrive as a surprise while a generic developer news feed produces nothing but noise. Read the stack first so relevance is grounded in what is actually depended on, then prefer a few findings that would change something over broad coverage.

name: Agent platform error ingestion
description: Some agent failures announce themselves and some just stop, and a record built only from the announcements is missing exactly the failures nobody noticed. Catch failures both ways at once and normalise them into one record shape, deciding what is genuinely a repeat of something already recorded rather than a second failure.

name: Conversion experiment program digest
description: An optimisation program that only communicates when something wins leaves its owner unable to tell a quiet period from a stalled one. Compose one honest account of where the whole program stands, including the uncertainty, rather than reporting only the parts that look like progress.

name: Regulatory acceptance mapping to controls and evidence
description: A compliance claim costs nothing to write and everything to defend. The usual document lists regulations beside the words compliant or in progress, which tells a reader neither what satisfies the requirement nor where to look for proof, and the first person to ask for the proof discovers that half the rows were intentions. The reference this is written against solved it with a shape rather than a longer document: one table, one artefact path per requirement, and a named gap written in wherever no artefact exists. Its own evidence pack does exactly that for DORA, mapping Art. 5 and 6 to `docs/bcp/dora-ictrm.md` and `docs/threat-models/`, Art. 8 to per service SBOMs and a third party register, Art. 9 to policy authorization and pull request time vulnerability checks, and Art. 11(3)(c) to `docs/bcp/dr-test-log.md`, and it names four gaps rather than rounding them up. Break one named regulation into requirements small enough that a single control can answer each, decide which control does answer it, then go and look for the artefact that would evidence that control to somebody who does not trust you. A requirement whose artefact exists becomes a row. A requirement whose artefact does not exist yet becomes a named gap with what would close it, never a row with an intention in the evidence column, because a matrix is only worth reading if its rows are the ones that could survive being checked.

name: Issue handling trend review
description: A count of resolved issues says nothing about whether the queue is getting better. Without a comparison nobody can tell a good period from a bad one, and the same totals get restated until they stop being read. Compare rather than count: state what moved since the last account, and be explicit about which figure came from the live source and which from local state.

name: Website conversion gap audit
description: A site can look finished and still lose every visitor at the same place, and a list of everything imperfect tells the owner nothing about which gap is costing them. Judge each category by what the gap costs in visitors or ranking position rather than in taste, comparing the site against what it itself scored last time.

name: Payment event scoring for churn and expansion
description: An account sliding toward churn, or ready to expand, is visible in payment behaviour long before it shows up in a business review, and a failed payment has a short window in which it can still be recovered. Turn each event into a movement in that account's risk and readiness scores, decide whether the movement crosses a band worth telling someone about, and separate a transient failure the provider will retry from one that needs a person.

name: Audio briefing production
description: An approved script is not a listenable briefing, and hand editing every segment into one track is the step that stops briefings from shipping regularly. Synthesize each segment as speech, join the segments into one coherent track with deliberate pacing between them, and judge the result against the runtime the script promised before calling it finished.

name: Unsigned contract signature chasing
description: A contract sitting unsigned costs whatever it was going to be worth, and chasing it is a relationship: too few nudges and it dies quietly, too many and the counterparty stops reading anything you send. Judge when a signer has waited long enough to be nudged again given how they normally respond, and when chasing has stopped working and the contract belongs to a person instead.

name: Code change implementation and review follow-through
description: An accepted item that turns into a change nobody can review, or a review comment that gets coded around rather than answered, costs more than the item was worth. Make the change scoped to what was accepted and let the repository's own checks be the standard, then answer review feedback the way a careful engineer would, escalating objections to the approach rather than patching them away.

name: Service self declaration and lineage maintenance
description: What a service holds, where it holds it, how long it must keep it and who it reads from are questions asked at the worst possible moments: during an incident, during an audit, and when a schema changes under a consumer nobody knew existed. Answered from a hand written architecture document they are answered wrongly, because a document describing seventy odd services has already drifted from the directory listing by the time anyone rereads it. And a declaration nobody checks is worse than no declaration at all: it carries the authority of a fact while being a claim, and the lineage edge it names may have been deleted a year ago. Keep one small declaration per service holding only the facts a person decides and a build cannot derive: the data domain it belongs to, its primary store and the database it owns, the classification of what it holds, its retention period, and its lineage in both directions with the relation type and what flows across each edge. Then hold every declared edge against the code, because a declaration whose edges nobody verifies is a claim wearing a fact's clothes.

name: Live database question answering
description: People who need a number wait for whoever can write the query, and the person who can write it spends their week writing them. Opening the database directly instead trades one problem for a worse one. Decide what is actually being asked, whether it can be answered safely inside the agreed boundary, and refuse with a reason rather than guessing or quietly narrowing it.

name: Congressional stock disclosure coverage
description: Disclosure filings arrive on their own schedule and in bursts, so anyone watching them by hand either checks constantly or misses the window in which a filing still means something. Advance a cursor over filings rather than rescanning a fixed window, match them against the declared sectors and holdings, and treat an unusual concentration in one sector as the finding rather than any single filing.

name: Weighted decision analysis and checkpoint review
description: A hard choice gets made on the criteria that were loudest that day, with nothing written down that could later prove it wrong, so nobody can tell afterwards whether it worked. Force the alternatives into the open, weigh them on criteria the requester recognises rather than generic ones, and get a kill criterion and a checkpoint written while they are still willing to name one.

name: Workforce planning across a project portfolio
description: Work stalls for a reason nobody writes down: a responsibility that has no holder. Each project owner feels it locally and asks for help in their own words, so the same missing role gets requested three times under three names while a role that was hired for work that has since ended keeps its seat. Nothing reads the asks together, nothing compares them against what the goals are actually doing, and a request written as a job title carries none of the evidence a hiring system would need to compose anything useful from it. Decide which roles the workspace is actually missing, by reading the owners' asks against the evidence in the goals rather than taking each ask at face value, and describe each real gap as the work it is: what has to be done, what evidence says it is not being done now, how anyone would know the role succeeded, and what the role is allowed and not allowed to touch. Send that to the hiring system, judge what comes back against the need as written, and retire the roles whose work has ended.

name: Threat model and evidence custody for a money path project
description: This work is for money path projects only, and it says so because the cost of holding it everywhere is that it is held nowhere. A threat model is written once, at the moment somebody asks for one, and then the service it describes keeps moving: a new caller, a token that now crosses a boundary it did not cross before, a queue that a second consumer joined. The document does not move with it, so within two quarters the model describes a system that no longer exists while still reading as current. The same happens to the evidence a project claims: a control is named, the artefact behind it was never produced, and nobody notices because a claim and an artefact look identical in a list. Keep a current threat model for every money path service in this project, and treat a change that moves a trust boundary as a change to the model in the same act rather than as a follow up. Then check the models against reality in the other direction: every claim a model makes about a control has to resolve to something that exists, and every piece of evidence this project has promised has to be an artefact somebody can open, or be written down as a named gap.

name: Watchlist technical signal digest
description: Indicator readings on a watchlist produce a verdict per ticker and no reasoning, so nobody can tell afterwards whether the method worked or whether one lucky call carried it. State a signal only when the indicators behind it agree enough to justify it, report the disagreement when they do not, and never fabricate a figure for a ticker the sources could not cover.

name: Database anomaly incident diagnosis
description: A serious database deviation reaches a person as an alarm and nothing else, so the first hour goes into reconstructing evidence that has already stopped existing. Capture the evidence while it is still there, correlate what moved together, and offer a hypothesis carrying the confidence it actually deserves rather than the confidence that would be reassuring.

name: Support request SLA watch and escalation
description: Somebody who asked for help is waiting, and nobody knows it. A breach discovered after the fact is only a report; the same information an hour earlier would have been a save. Judge which requests are entering their risk window before they breach, and which genuinely need a person, since escalating everything is as bad as escalating nothing.

name: Paid and organic keyword cannibalization watch
description: Money is spent bidding on terms the site already wins organically, and because the two numbers live in different systems nobody ever puts them side by side. Cross reference the two and judge where the paid spend is buying traffic that was already arriving, putting a number on what that is costing.

name: Decision record rot watch
description: A decision stays presented as current long after the thing it assumed stopped being true, and the reader who arrives at the old record has no way to tell. Watch the assumptions rather than the dates, and never silently reaffirm: if nothing has changed, say that nothing has changed.

name: Codebase static analysis sweep
description: Dead code, duplication and eroded module boundaries are cheap to find with a tool and expensive to maintain forever, and the tool's output dies in a terminal instead of becoming work. Run the tool faithfully and turn its output into work one finding at a time, without scoring or summarising past what it actually found, and learn which unreferenced code is deliberate.

name: Community discussion trend digest
description: The communities where a product's users talk about it move faster than anyone can read, and a digest that pads itself to look consistent teaches its readers to skip it. Cluster genuinely new discussion into the few themes that actually ran, label the sentiment honestly, and ship fewer themes on a quiet day rather than stretching thin material.

name: Contract envelope event sync
description: A contract tracker that is updated by hand is out of date by definition, and the gap is invisible: a contract stalled at review looks the same as one merely open, and a decline is discovered when somebody asks. Reconstruct the true sequence when events arrive twice or out of order, write the tracker so it says what is actually true, and decide which changes are worth interrupting someone over.

name: Access request intake and triage
description: Access requests arrive as ordinary messages among everything else, so the same ask gets entered twice, or read once and forgotten, and the record of who asked for what stops being something anyone would defend. Decide what each message is really asking for, whether it has already been captured, and how much privilege it carries, because that classification is what later decides whether a person has to say yes.

name: Technical decision capture
description: Consequential choices get made in conversation and never written down, so a year later nobody can tell what constraint forced the decision or what the alternatives were, and the choice gets relitigated from scratch. Establish the constraint that forced the choice and the alternatives that lost, pushing back when what arrives is too thin to be useful later rather than filing it anyway.

name: Correspondence activity digest
description: Whoever runs an assisted-reply pipeline cannot tell whether it is keeping pace without opening every channel, and the thing most worth knowing, how much is still waiting on a human, is the thing least visible. Assemble a calm status readout that answers whether replies are keeping pace and where attention is needed, without ever requiring an action to be useful.

name: Survey response theme and sentiment analysis
description: Feedback read one batch at a time turns a loud response into a trend and a quietly recurring one into nothing, and a thin batch read eagerly produces a confident conclusion the data does not support. Read for themes rather than scores, weight by how many said it and how consistently, and buffer rather than analyse when the batch is too thin to mean anything.

name: Contract renewal window watch
description: Renewal clocks run whether anyone is watching or not. A contract auto renews on terms nobody re-negotiated, or lapses because the notice window closed while it was still on somebody's list. Judge which windows are close enough to act on, raise them while a decision is still possible, and keep a current answer to what renews next and what has changed since the last time anyone asked.

name: Deploy regression correlation
description: When errors jump, whoever is on call starts from zero on the question that matters most, which is what changed just before, and the answer is sitting in the deploy list nobody cross referenced. Decide which error jumps are close enough to a deploy to be named as its regression, and which are merely near it in time and must be labelled as no more than possibly related.

name: Content source health tracking
description: A source that has quietly stopped yielding anything looks identical to a quiet one, so dead entries stay on a follow list forever and spend budget every pass. Distinguish a source that is quiet from a source that is broken by requiring a clear run of failures before saying anything, then recommend removal rather than continuing to poll.

name: Architecture decision records with decision status split from delivery status
description: A decision record says accepted and everyone downstream reads it as built. They are two different facts with two different owners and two different dates, and collapsing them costs twice: a compliance answer cites an accepted decision whose implementation was never deployed, and a team builds against a control that exists only in a document. This is not hypothetical. In the reference this work is designed against, one decision stands accepted while the compliance mapping that reads it records its topology as not deployed, and an independent review control reads restored, narrowed to a fraction of the fleet, and advisory rather than required, while the decision behind it says only that it was accepted. Record the decision and its delivery as two statuses that move independently and carry their own dates. Accepted says a choice was made and by whom; delivered says how much of it exists in the code and what proves it. Revisit the second whenever the code moves, name the scope wherever delivery covered less than the decision decided, and never let the first status imply the second.

name: Database performance baseline monitoring
description: A database degrades against its own normal long before it crosses any generic threshold, so a team watching fixed numbers either misses the degradation or is trained by false alarms to ignore the ones that matter. Judge each sample against what this database actually does at this hour of this day, and decide whether a move is worth a glance, worth waking someone, or worth nothing at all.

name: Audio briefing script drafting
description: Source material read aloud verbatim does not hold a listener, and discovering that after paying for synthesis is the expensive way to find out. Find the headline finding, the facts that carry it, the tensions worth airing and the questions left open, then shape them into two host turns that pace correctly when spoken rather than when read.

name: Codebase stewardship by a maintenance worker the owner scopes
description: A project that only ever adds behaviour accrues the debt nobody was asked to pay: modules that grew past the shape they were designed for, three copies of one helper, a build that takes a minute longer each month, dependencies pinned to versions with known holes, and test suites that pass while covering less than they did. None of it is an accepted idea, because nobody files 'the code is worse than it needs to be' as a finding, and the owner's delivery capacity is spent on the ideas that were filed. The work is real, mechanical, and well suited to a cheaper engine than the one that decides what the project is for. Carry ONE bounded maintenance scope the owner wrote: a refactor that keeps behaviour, a structural rebalance of files and modules, a technical-design upgrade the owner named, a dependency or toolchain move, or a coverage or build-time repair. Read the code and the gates before touching anything, make the change on its own branch in small commits, keep every test and gate green without editing a gate or deleting a test, and stop at the scope's edge with a note for the owner about what lies past it.

name: Codebase architecture review
description: Structural problems cost the most and announce themselves the least, and by the time an eroded boundary or an unowned subsystem is obvious it is an incident rather than a proposal. Read for the structural problems that will cost most later and decide which few are worth competing with product work, treating settled decisions as constraints rather than as things to reopen.

name: Idea architecture and feasibility verdict
description: An idea reaches a ranking queue carrying only its own enthusiasm, so whoever ranks it has to work out for themselves who it helps, what it costs and whether the architecture even allows it. Add the judgement the idea is missing from both the product and the architectural side, being willing to conclude that it should not be done and saying why in terms a later scan can respect.

name: Release record and version bump
description: A version number chosen from the wording of a commit message is a claim about compatibility that nobody checked, and a changelog written afterwards is written from memory. Choose the version step from what the change actually does to callers rather than from how it was described, and keep version, changelog and notes consistent with that choice.

name: Codebase security scan
description: A generic vulnerability list is read once and ignored afterwards, because it names problems without naming what to do about them or which ones actually matter here. Treat dependency vulnerabilities, exposed secrets and risky code patterns as three genuinely different questions, and rank what is found by real severity with a fix a developer could apply without further research.

name: Approved draft channel publishing
description: Approved work sits unpublished, and the person who approved it has no way to tell whether their decision reached the world. Carry the approved draft through to actually being live or scheduled on the channel it was approved for, and report what happened with a link or a time.

name: Conversion experiment significance watch
description: An experiment called early is worse than no experiment, because the wrong variant then ships with the authority of a measurement behind it. Decide for each experiment whether it has actually earned a verdict yet, watching for signs the measurement itself is broken, and propose what to do rather than doing it.

name: Post-incident review and prevention proposals
description: The only lasting product of an incident is what was learned from it, and that evaporates within days unless somebody writes it while responders can still correct it. Write an honest account of what happened, preferring a stated unknown cause to a plausible invented one, and decide when a cause has returned often enough that another review is the wrong response.

name: Scope reflection on personas' own proposals and lessons
description: The people doing the work are the first to see where their scope is wrong, and in an organisation of agents they say so in writing: a proposal to take on a responsibility nobody holds, to give one up, to split one that turned out to be two. Those proposals then sit unread, because reading them is nobody's job and answering one means deciding whether it changes a single charter or the whole design. The same happens to lessons: each one is filed where it was learned, so the next holder of the same work learns it again from scratch. Read what the workers proposed about their own scope and decide, for each one, what it would actually change: a charter, the design, a gate, or nothing. A gate is the verdict whenever the lesson is mechanical and would otherwise be a paragraph nobody reads at the moment it matters, because a rule that generalises should refuse the mistake rather than describe it. Apply the ones that hold, decline the rest with a reason the proposer can argue with, and separate the lessons that only apply where they were learned from the ones any holder of that work would want, promoting only the second kind.

name: Email inbox attention digest
description: Reading every unread message to find the few that matter costs more attention than the messages themselves, and a digest ranked by recency does not save any of it. Rank by a real signal, who the reader actually answers combined with what the message says, and surface a short accurate list rather than a complete one.

name: Agent reliability reporting
description: Whether a fleet of agents is getting more or less reliable is usually a feeling formed from whichever incident was most recent, which is exactly the wrong basis for deciding what to fix. Turn the record into per agent error rate and time to resolution with movement against the previous window, and rank the recommendations rather than listing the errors.

name: Support escalation pattern review
description: A support function that only reports its escalations absorbs the same pain forever. The cause that produced fifty tickets is described fifty times and fixed never. Name the causes behind recurring escalations rather than restating the escalations, decide which have a fixable root, and file those as work instead of reporting them again.

name: Acceptance certification by representative users across two levels
description: A project's own checks answer whether the code does what its authors meant. Nothing in them answers whether a representative user can finish the job they came for, at a standard a senior person in that role would accept. So a project accumulates green gates and shipping waves while a journey nobody walks end to end has been broken for a month. The two honest failures are opposite and both common: certifying only against a model of the surface, which is cheap and never touches the running system, and certifying only in a live browser, which is slow enough that it happens once and then never again. Certify the project's journeys through the eyes of its representative users at two levels with different costs and different truth. Run the cheap theoretical level over the surface the code describes after every merged wave, because it is affordable often enough to catch a regression the week it lands. Run the empirical level against the running system once per act, because it is the only level that can contradict the first one. Judge each journey through its user's own lens rather than against a feature list, and file every finding as an item the project delivers.

name: Money path service certification against a declared contract
description: A service carrying nine of its ten obligations reads exactly like one carrying ten, and the difference only shows on the day the missing one was the one that mattered. The obligations that protect money are the ones nobody notices missing: a write endpoint that shipped without an idempotency key, a domain layer that quietly took a framework dependency, a migration with no rollback note, a timestamp read from the wall clock instead of an injected one. The reference this work is written against states the cost in the rationale of its own gate `idempotency-coverage-money-path`: a duplicate POST on a money path endpoint is a double debit, and without a ratchet a new endpoint ships without a key and nothing objects. Read one service against the contract its own project declared, obligation by obligation, and give each one a verdict backed by the file that carries it or the absence that proves it missing. Keep three verdicts apart rather than two: carried, absent, and not checkable from here, because a certification that cannot tell absent from unlooked at is worth nothing. File every gap as an idea naming the obligation it violates, and change no code, because a reader that repairs what it finds stops being able to report what it found.

name: Web content performance review
description: Movement in a product's own numbers goes unnoticed until it is too late to act on, and a table of metrics with no interpretation is not a read on anything. Judge each move against what this product normally does rather than a fixed threshold, allowing a wider band for low volume pages, and end in a proposal or an explicit nothing worth doing.

name: Service contract stewardship across a project's merge waves
description: A project agrees what every one of its services must carry, and then ships anyway. The list lives in a design document, the services are built by different hands weeks apart, and nothing compares the two until an audit or an incident does it. Each missing piece is individually small, which is exactly why none of them is ever the reason to stop: a service without a rollback note, one whose published contract no longer matches the routes it serves, one whose events go out with no consumer anywhere. The obligations are only visible together, and only just before something merges, because after the merge the project has already agreed to carry them. Before a wave of work merges, read every service in the project against the contract the project declared, obligation by obligation, and decide for each service whether it is certified, certified with named gaps, or not certified at all. File each missing obligation as an idea naming the obligation it violates and the service it belongs to, rather than fixing it inside the certification. Refuse to certify against a contract that does not exist: an undeclared contract is the finding, and the wave stops on it.

name: Infrastructure metrics scan
description: Infrastructure usually fails by drifting away from its own recent normal, not by crossing a memorable round number, so a watch built on absolute thresholds sees the failure late or not at all. Compare each metric against its own baseline instead of a shared static threshold, and let past triage decisions decide how loudly a familiar deviation is reported.

name: Production error issue filter
description: Root cause analysis is expensive per issue, so anything that reaches it must be worth investigating; a filter that passes everything makes the analysis step useless. Apply the occurrence floor and the learned noise patterns to decide which issues are worth an investigation, without forming an opinion about what caused them.

name: Gate authorship as a project owner's answer to a recurring defect
description: A defect happens, gets fixed, and the fix ends as a sentence: a line in a conventions file, a paragraph in a review, a lesson on a charter. Then it happens again, to a different author who never read the sentence, and the second fix produces a second sentence. Prose is read by the people who already agree with it, which is why the only reader a written rule reliably reaches is its author. Meanwhile the manifest of mechanical checks belongs to another project, so writing into it means asking somebody else, and asking is exactly the step that a note lets you skip. Decide which of this project's recurring defects is a rule rather than an accident, and answer it with a check in the shared manifest rather than another sentence. That means proving recurrence before proposing, deciding whether the rule generalises past this project or belongs only here, carrying the proposal to whoever owns the manifest instead of writing into their project unasked, and then keeping the check alive afterwards: honouring its review date, graduating it from advisory to enforced or retiring it, and noticing when it has quietly stopped finding anything.

name: Knowledge base content curation
description: Content saved without judgment turns a knowledge base into a pile: everything is in there, nothing is findable later, and the same source has three pages. Judge whether the content is actually worth adding, then write a summary at the depth a later reader needs and find the cross-references that make the page discoverable rather than merely filed.

name: Access request approval chain
description: A request nobody decided looks exactly like one that was denied, and the person waiting cannot tell which. Left alone, silence becomes the way privileged access gets granted. Carry each request to an explicit approved, denied or escalated verdict, judging when a quiet approver has become an escalation and holding anything high privilege for a person to say yes out loud.

name: Work candidate triage gate
description: Anything that generates candidates will eventually generate more than anyone can absorb, and without one gate the low value ones are either built or silently dropped, both of which are worse than a decision. Give a person enough context to accept, reject or defer without further digging, and turn what they decide into a signal the upstream source learns from.

name: Project portfolio composition from a solution design
description: A solution design that never becomes projects is a drawing. The step from one to the other is where portfolios go wrong quietly: a service in the design that nobody created a home for, a repository that exists on disk but was never registered so no persona can reach it, a project standing with no owner because adoption was left for later, two projects that both believe they own the same context, and a project created with no goal at all, whose team then invents its own direction from whatever it can see. Turn the design into a portfolio that matches it: create each missing repository and register it as a project in the workspace in one act, have each project declare itself in a machine readable file the moment it exists, adopt an App Master on each with the charters that context actually needs, set each project's first goals from the design's own words, then read the portfolio back against the design and resolve every orphan, every duplicate owner and every project standing without direction.

name: Cloud spend threshold watch
description: A budget is breached in the middle of a billing period, but nobody finds out until reconciliation, by which point the spend is already committed. Project the likely end-of-period total from the run rate and judge the trajectory rather than today's number, then stay quiet unless the projection or the actual crosses the threshold.

name: Cloud cost and resource reporting
description: Cloud cost drifts in small per-service increments that no single invoice line explains, so a rise is normally discovered at the invoice and then cannot be attributed to anything. Compare each service against its own baseline, decide which moves are worth naming and which are the expected consequence of a change that was made on purpose, and report the whole picture either way.

name: Database row change watch
description: Row level change streams are almost entirely the product working correctly, so a watch that relays them all trains its audience to ignore it and hides the few changes that should never have happened. Judge which changes are genuinely off against what this data normally does, and decide who, if anyone, needs to hear about each one and in how much detail.

name: Under-covered equity discovery by sector
description: Screens produce names that clear a mechanical filter and nothing more, so the output looks like research while carrying no thesis anyone could argue with. Require all three legs, thin coverage, a technical case, and a real catalyst, and treat two out of three as a rejection rather than a weaker recommendation.

name: Webhook classification and routing
description: Incoming events arrive in every shape from every system, and without one door that classifies and fans them out they either reach nobody or reach everybody. Classify the payload accurately enough that the right rule applies, transform it for each destination it names, and treat losing an event as the one unacceptable outcome.

name: Release candidate review and approval
description: Merged work either sits unreleased for no reason anybody could state, or gets tagged on a day of the week whether or not the suite is green and whether or not there is anything worth shipping. Decide whether what has accumulated is worth releasing at all, prove it against the whole suite rather than the individual changes, and take it to a person to approve.

name: Load envelope authorship and measured ceiling reporting
description: Load targets are usually adjectives dressed as engineering. A system is said to handle a million users, and the number came from the ambition rather than from anything anybody ran, so it can never be met or missed. When a run does happen the second failure arrives: the percentiles are read from a run where a share of the requests never answered, which quietly removes the slowest work from the sample and reports a system faster than the one that exists. The reference this is written against puts the rule in every one of its read baselines, that a route which did not answer 200 invalidates the percentile, and asserts a failed request rate under 0.01 with a checks rate of exactly 1.0 beside it. State the target as five numbers before anything runs: how much data is seeded, what rate is sustained, for how long, at which latency percentile, and what error rate invalidates the result. Then run it, apply the error rule before reading a single percentile, and report the machine's own resource ceiling beside the latency figures, because a percentile with no ceiling next to it cannot be compared to any other run. Where a larger figure is wanted, derive it as arithmetic from what was measured and label it as arithmetic.

name: Goal direction and channel authority across projects
description: A design becomes real only through goals somebody set and direction somebody gave, and both fail in the same quiet way. Goals get written once at the start and then drift from the design nobody reread, so the projects work hard on the wrong thing. Direction is spoken in a register the listener cannot tell from a suggestion, so an instruction is treated as a thought and a thought is treated as an order. And when two projects want opposite things, each argues locally with the owner who cannot decide it, because the only reader who can see both is the one who never came back to look. Keep every project's goals traceable to the design and current against it, and speak into the shared channel with the register said out loud: a directive is an instruction that expects the work done, a request expects an answer, a note is context that expects nothing. Phrase a directive as an acceptance criterion drawn from a standard the domain already holds rather than as an outcome you want, because a criterion somebody else wrote can be met or missed and an outcome you phrased yourself can only be argued about. Then read what came back, chase the directives nobody answered, and decide the conflicts between projects that no single project can settle.

name: Feature walkthrough capture from the running app
description: A feature nobody can watch has to be explained by hand every time, and a walkthrough recorded from a guessed script shows screens the app does not produce. Read the code first so the walkthrough follows the path a real user takes, then drive that path live and pace the capture for a viewer rather than for the machine.

name: Newsletter issue curation and delivery
description: A newsletter assembled from whatever the feeds produced is a link dump, and subscribers stop opening it long before anyone notices the sources went stale. Judge which items are actually worth a subscriber's attention, group what belongs together, and write real commentary saying why each matters rather than restating the headline.

name: Gate authorship from a recurring defect
description: A defect that has happened twice will happen a third time, and the usual answer is a paragraph. The paragraph is read by the people who already knew, and the next author, who never read it, ships the same defect again. The mechanical answer fails differently and worse: a check written in a hurry passes forever, is never once seen to fail, and is trusted precisely because it has never objected to anything. The reference this is written against names that failure in its own manifest header, that a gate which has only ever passed is unfalsified, and answers it by running the proof of reachable failure before the check and skipping the check when that proof gives the wrong verdict. Decide what the occurrences have in common, and whether that common thing is checkable by a machine rather than by a reader's attention. Where it is, declare it as one entry in the project's manifest carrying four things a check cannot be trusted without: how many subjects it expects to find, the reason it exists in the words of the defect it prevents, a date it should be argued with again, and a proof that its failing state is reachable. Where it is not mechanically checkable, say so and leave it as prose rather than shipping a check that cannot fail.

name: Database anomaly baseline refresh
description: Anomaly detection is only as honest as the baseline behind it, and a baseline computed once quietly turns every ordinary business change into an anomaly and every real anomaly into normal. Recompute the distributions detection depends on from what the business has actually been doing recently, and decide whether the new numbers are trustworthy enough to replace the old ones.

name: Accepted idea delivery to the main branch
description: An accepted idea that nobody carries to the main branch is a decision that never happened, and the work already exists in pieces that each own a different hand-off: one triages, one implements, one gives a test verdict, one releases. Nothing owns the item's identity from accepted to merged, nothing re-checks the idea against the code as it stands before building it, and nothing looks afterwards to see whether the change did what the idea claimed. Carry one accepted item all the way to a reviewable, verified change on the main branch: re-validate it against the current code with the authority to decline and say why, derive the checklist that will prove it done, implement it in an isolated branch, let the repository's own checks and tests be the standard, deliver a pull request or a ready branch where no hosted review surface exists, and after the merge check the claim the idea made.

name: Database activity digest
description: A team that only ever sees individual database events has no sense of direction, and cannot tell a bad week from a normal one until something breaks. Turn the period's activity into one account that shows direction of change rather than a table of totals, and decide what a reader would actually act on.

name: Codebase latent defect hunt
description: The defects a careful reader would catch are found by users instead, because nobody has the time to read the code the way a reviewer would. Read like a reviewer and judge which of the things that look wrong are genuinely likely to break, filing few and real rather than many and speculative.

name: Source artifact repurposing for channels
description: Something published once reaches only the audience of the place it was published, and reformatting it by hand for every other channel is the work that quietly stops getting done. Produce what each channel actually needs from the source, as a rewrite grounded in that channel's own voice description rather than the same text reformatted.

name: Agent platform error classification
description: A raw failure record tells nobody what to do, and a forced classification into the nearest familiar bucket is worse than admitting the failure is new. Give the failure a category, a cause, a blast radius and a specific remediation, or say honestly that it is uncategorised rather than fitting it to the nearest bucket.

name: Knowledge base contradiction audit
description: Two articles covering the same ground and saying different things are both individually healthy: neither is stale, neither is orphaned. A per document audit cannot see the problem, and whoever reads one of them gets a confident wrong answer. Cluster articles that appear to cover the same ground, compare their bodies for genuine disagreement, and hand every pair to a person rather than deciding which one is right.

name: Knowledge base curation audit
description: A curated knowledge base degrades in ways nobody notices from inside it: pages nothing links to, and a taxonomy that has sprawled past the point where its tags mean anything. Find orphaned pages and near-duplicate tags, read them against earlier audits so a trend is visible, and propose rather than apply.

name: Paid and organic channel performance scan
description: Paid and organic performance sit in separate dashboards, so nobody reads them together and the findings that only exist between them are never found. Read both channels against what is normal for this account rather than against last period alone, and report degradation honestly when one source is unavailable.

name: Memory and knowledge base health audit
description: The layers an agent remembers through decay quietly: notes go stale, documents orphan from the code they described, articles start disagreeing with each other. Nothing fails, and trust in the whole system erodes instead. Find drift, staleness, orphans and contradiction, rank the findings by severity and recency, and hand every one to a person with a recommended action, never mutating a layer itself.

name: Harvested idea triage
description: A harvested idea that goes straight into feasibility analysis spends real effort before anyone has said it is wanted. Put the idea to a person for accept or reject before any analysis effort is spent on it, and let repeated rejections in a category suppress future harvesting of that category.

name: Threat model for a money path service
description: Most threat models are written once, at the moment somebody asked for one, and are wrong within a quarter. The model itself is rarely the problem: the problem is that the service kept moving and the model did not. A new caller, a new queue, a credential that started being read by something else, a boundary that used to be inside one process and is now a network hop, and the document still describes a system that no longer exists while carrying the authority of one that was reviewed. The reference this is written against treats a structured model as a definition of done artefact under ADR-0030 D2, at `docs/threat-models/<service>.md`, and its checker fails the pipeline if any money path service lacks a structured one; gate `threat-model-coverage` enforces that, and 45 models exist under it. Trace where this service's data crosses a boundary somebody else controls, work each crossing through the threat categories, and decide for each credible threat whether it is mitigated, deliberately accepted or still open, saying who accepted what. Write it in the structured form the project can check rather than as prose. Then do the part the first authoring never covers: read every change to the service for a moved trust boundary, and reopen the model in the same change that moved it, because a model updated later is a model that was wrong in between.

name: Codebase test coverage advance
description: The parts of a codebase that would hurt most if they broke are usually the parts nobody got round to testing, and a coverage percentage says nothing about which parts those are. Pick the next area actually worth covering rather than the one that moves the percentage most, write tests in the conventions already present, and prove they pass.

name: Pull request test verdict
description: A change reaches the main branch on the strength of somebody's belief that the tests would pass, and the one time that belief is wrong is the time it matters. Run the change in isolation from anyone else's working tree and let the real result, not assumption, decide between approving, asking for changes, and handing it on with the failure named.

name: Skill library audit and proposal
description: A library of written procedures drifts away from the code it describes and accumulates entries nobody has used in months, and neither drift nor disuse announces itself. Turn genuine drift or genuine disuse into a proposal a person can approve or reject, capped tightly enough that the review queue stays readable.

name: Project KPI and coverage stewardship
description: A project's context map, use cases and KPIs decay quietly: contexts nobody has scanned since the code moved, groups carrying no KPI at all, KPIs with a target and no measurement behind it, and a backlog that is either empty or full of items nobody has looked at in months. None of it announces itself, because each number lives on a different screen and no single reading puts them beside each other. Keep the project's measurement loop honest and moving: read the coverage, decide which gap this cycle is worth closing, populate the backlog with concrete items that carry their evidence, get them executed through the delivery loop, and back-measure so every claim that something improved is a number that moved rather than a description of work done.

name: Original 2D art generation and curation
description: A generated art library grows into noise unless somebody decides what stays, and an agent that never learns from those decisions keeps producing the same rejected work. Conceive a direction that has not been tried, generate work in it, and present each piece for an explicit keep or discard decision rather than assuming taste.

name: Conversion variant hypothesis proposals
description: Pages underperform quietly, and the ideas offered for them are usually generic best practice that would apply to any site and therefore explains nothing about this one. Rank pages by how far below their own baseline they sit and write a small number of hypotheses specific to what is actually underperforming on each, each naming what it expects to move.

name: Free promotion surface discovery
description: Lists of places to promote a product are generic by default, which means they fit any product and are therefore worth nothing to this one. Find the specific forums, communities, newsletters and directories where this product's actual users already gather, offering few and specific rather than many and plausible.

name: Per channel writing voice profiling
description: Drafts written without a written description of how this person sounds read like nobody, and the same correction gets made on every draft forever because nothing records it. Derive from real examples how they open, how long their sentences run, what words they never use and how they close, and write it down concretely enough that a draft can be checked against it.

name: Competitor conversion and positioning comparison
description: A snapshot of where competitors stand today says nothing about which direction anyone is moving, and a comparison scored on a different yardstick than the home site means nothing at all. Read what has changed since the last look, a feature that appeared, pricing that moved, a claim withdrawn, and score it on the identical categories so the comparison is honest.

name: Database schema picture refresh
description: Anything answering questions about a database works from a cached picture of its structure. When the real database moves and the picture does not, the answers stay confident and become wrong, which is worse than failing. Decide whether a fresh read is trustworthy enough to replace what is held, since a bad read that overwrites a good picture does more damage than a stale one.

name: Revenue signal alerting and outreach
description: Money that was going to arrive and did not, and accounts drifting toward leaving or ready to grow, all fail quietly. The window in which any of them can still be acted on is short, and by the time it shows up in a revenue report it has closed. Separate a signal that will resolve on its own from one that needs a person, raise it once with its cause in the provider's own terms, and never contact a customer on the operator's behalf unless he has explicitly said that is wanted.

name: Form lead intake and scoring
description: A form submission that is recorded twice, scored against a generic rubric, or not recorded at all costs a real opportunity, and none of those failures announce themselves. Work out who this is and whether they matter, judged against how this business actually sells rather than a generic rubric, and record it exactly once whether or not they have been seen before.

name: Scouted opportunity triage
description: A discovered opportunity that goes straight to an implementation agent spends build effort on something nobody asked for. Put the opportunity to a person with enough context to decide, and let the rejection reasons train which topics stop being surfaced.

name: Content metrics anomaly check
description: Waiting for the end of a period to discover something moved wastes the half of the period in which it could still have been acted on. Compare where the numbers actually are against where the baseline says they should be by now, and say nothing at all when they are tracking normally.

name: Product design brief authoring
description: Without one written description of how a product should look, every piece of visual work is judged against a different unstated standard and none of it composes. Name concrete colour roles, type treatment and layout direction rather than adjectives, taking the adopter's own brief verbatim where one exists and doing the extraction work only where one does not.

name: Application error scan
description: An error list that shows the same dismissed pattern every day teaches its readers to skim, and the one new error that matters goes past unread with the rest. Classify each error's severity from the data and from the triage history together, so a signature dismissed repeatedly quietly drops without anyone having to dismiss it again.

name: Abuse path smoke suite where the rejection is the subject
description: A test suite proves the happy path and then stops, so the only requests anybody exercises are the ones a well behaved client sends. The rejection path is the one an attacker walks and the one nobody tests, and it fails in two directions at once: a route that answers a request carrying no credential has already leaked, and a route that answers a malformed one with a server error has told the caller that the guard was never reached. Worse than either, a suite of invalid requests that has only ever been green has never been shown to detect anything, so its greenness is evidence of nothing at all. Build a suite in which every request is invalid by construction, and assert the exact status class each abuse must produce rather than asserting that nothing broke. A 200 on any probe is a finding and a 5xx on any probe is a finding, because the first means the guard did not run and the second means something behind it answered instead. Then prove the suite itself by weakening one route on purpose and watching it turn red.

name: Marketing optimization proposals
description: Marketing advice that would apply to any account regardless of its data is not doing anything, and a list too long to evaluate is refused wholesale rather than judged. Turn the reading into a small number of specific changes worth making, each carrying the data point that argues for it and an honest estimate of what it is worth.

name: On brand visual asset production
description: Surfaces ship with placeholder or stock visuals because making something that belongs to this specific product is slower than shipping without it. Compose the work from the brief rather than from scratch, judge it against the brief before showing it to anyone, and iterate a small fixed number of times rather than indefinitely.

name: Codebase feasibility analysis
description: Effort and benefit estimates made without opening the code are guesses that read like facts, and a backlog built from them is a backlog nobody can plan against. Let the code actually found, or its absence, drive the effort and benefit call, marking feasibility unknown rather than low when the search returns nothing.

name: Cross-project progress briefing
description: Someone running several projects at once loses the picture of which ones moved and which quietly stopped, and reconstructing it by hand costs more attention than the answer is worth. Report the difference since the last briefing rather than the current state, leading with the uncomfortable item, and ground every claim in something observable rather than in an earlier summary.

name: Decision record to code linking
description: A decision record that cannot be traced to the change that implemented it becomes a document nobody trusts, and a change that quietly contradicts a standing decision is invisible. Confirm a candidate link before recording it, because a wrong link is worse than a missing one, and raise a change that contradicts a standing decision rather than filing it as support for that decision.

name: Cross-workflow error pattern detection
description: One outage arrives as a dozen unrelated looking alerts across a dozen agents, and whoever is on call spends the first stretch working out that it is one thing. Recognise when separate failures are one thing, whether by repetition, by cascade, by clustering in time, or by a shared service, and decide whether an active pattern has changed enough to be worth saying again.

name: Survey insight report delivery
description: A completed feedback analysis that nobody receives, or that leaves the baseline untouched, means the next analysis compares against stale ground and the work is done twice. Turn the analysis into something a person receives and can act on, raising priority when a high-severity anomaly is present, then move the baselines so the next comparison is against fresh ground.

name: Incident capture and classification
description: One event usually gets reported several times by several people, and severity gets argued down once the pressure passes, so the record of what happened stops matching what happened. Decide whether this is a new incident or another report of one already open, and set severity from impact on real users or real work rather than from the tone of the report.

name: Cloud billing access failure alerting
description: A spend watch that cannot read billing looks exactly like a spend watch that found nothing wrong, so an outage quietly becomes weeks of unmeasured cost. Name the specific failure mode, expired credentials, a rate limit, a partial period, or an empty billing response, and give the next step for that provider rather than a generic error notice.

name: Contract intake and risk analysis
description: Contracts get signed on the strength of whoever had time to read them. Unfavourable terms, missing protections and clauses that are out of line with what this counterparty has signed before go unmentioned because nobody compared. Judge the contract on terms, money, obligations and risk, with this counterparty's own prior contracts as the market baseline, and refuse to analyse a document that is unreadable, partial, or an amendment whose original is missing.

name: Inbound message triage across channels
description: Messages arrive across several channels at once, and anything that needs a reply is as likely to be missed in the quiet channel as in the loud one. Log each message once, classify its urgency and intent well enough that the reply-needed flag can be trusted by whatever acts on it, and keep going on the channels that still work when one fails.

name: Codebase improvement backlog scan
description: The work a codebase most needs is written down inside it, in markers, hotspots and deprecated calls that nobody reads, and it never reaches the place where work is chosen. Decide what is genuinely worth fixing and describe each one well enough that a person can accept or reject it in seconds, without implementing anything.

name: Contract obligation and deadline watch
description: A contract's consequences are carried by dates that live inside it: notice windows, obligation due dates, warranty expiries. Nobody re-reads a signed contract to find them, so they arrive as surprises. Decide which dates are close enough to matter, how urgent each has become, and who can actually act, without raising the same date at the same urgency twice.

name: Content feed intake for curation
description: A feed sweep that reprocesses what it has already seen, or that dumps an unbounded batch into curation, costs more in reprocessing and quota than the new items are worth. Deduplicate and age-filter before anything reaches curation, and respect the per-run cap so the most recent items win when a feed floods.

name: Enterprise solution design across a workspace
description: An owner states a goal in the language of the business and the work starts anyway, one repository at a time, with nobody holding the whole. Two teams then own the same data under different names, a responsibility nobody claimed turns out to belong to everyone, the integration style is decided by whichever service was written first, and the load the system was supposed to carry is discovered at the end. None of that is visible from inside a single project, because a boundary is only wrong when seen against the boundary beside it. Decide where the seams of the system fall: which bounded contexts exist, which services carry which responsibility, who owns each piece of data, how the parts talk to each other and how much of that is asynchronous, what the non functional envelope is, and what is deliberately out of scope. Name each context against an external ontology the domain already has, so a boundary can be argued against something other than taste, and designate which parts of the system carry value that cannot be recreated, because those parts earn obligations the rest do not. Hold the design against reality as the projects build, and revise it when their evidence contradicts a boundary rather than defending the drawing.

name: Feature announcement video production
description: Shipped features go unannounced because a short video costs a script, a voice and a render, and getting any one of them wrong late means redoing all three. Settle the script and visual strategy and get them approved before anything is synthesized or rendered, then keep rework scoped to the stage that was actually wrong.

name: Database health check
description: A connection pool filling up, a slow query count climbing, or replication falling behind is a performance indicator for days before it is an outage, and nobody looks until it is the outage. Compare each health signal against its own recent history rather than a fixed number, and decide which movements are worth reporting and which are the database working normally.

name: Source-grounded error root cause analysis
description: A root cause report written from the stack trace alone restates what the reader already has, and the person triaging still has to open the code themselves. Read the actual code at the error location, trace who calls it, and decide which of several plausible causes the evidence supports, ranking the resolutions by what each would cost.

name: Event routing rule management
description: Routing rules are edited in a file by hand or not at all, so they drift from what anyone actually wants and conflicts between them are discovered by an event going to the wrong place. Translate the instruction into a correct rule, catch when it conflicts with one already configured, and ask one clarifying question rather than guessing.
